newsitem.title: USA: Durco to acquire BW/IP in stock swap.
newsitem.headline: Durco to acquire BW/IP in stock swap.

text.p: Durco International Inc. has agreed to acquire BW/IP Inc., another industrial manufacturing company, in a stock swap valued at about $440.2 million.

Both companies are leading makers of pumps, seals and valves, as well as fluid handling and control equipment. The combined company would have a market capitalisation of about $1.2 billion and annual sales of about $1.1 billion.
Under the agreement, Durco will offer 0.6968 share of its common stock for each of Long Beach, Calif.-based BW/IP's 24.3 million shares outstanding in a pooling of interests.
Durco's stock fell 25 cents to $26.375 on Nasdaq in afternoon trading. BW/IP stock fell 87.5 cents to $18.75 on the New York Stock Exchange.
While Durco shareholders will retain their current shares, the merged company will operate under a new name, to be announced before the deal closes.
"By merging ... we are creating the most cost-effective organisation possible and adding value for shareholders of both companies," said BW/IP Chairman Bernard Rethore.
Durco said the deal will result in between $35 million and $45 million of cost savings over the next three years.
The combined company is expected to pay dividends consistent with Dayton, Ohio-based Durco's recent dividends of about 56 cents per share per year, they said.
Rethore will become chairman and chief executive of the combined company, and Durco Chairman, President and Chief Executive William Jordan will become president and chief operating officer.
The new company's board will have 11 members, including five designated by Durco, four by BW/IP and two not affiliated with either company.
The deal is subject to approval by Durco and BW/IP shareholders at meetings that are expected to be held over the summer, and anti-trust approval.
The companies have granted each other options to buy 19.9 percent of each other's common stock if the deal does not close under certain circumstances.
